write.desc: This topic is about what it means for a function to be continuous at a point and on a set, the equivalent ways of saying it (epsilon-delta, limits, sequences, open sets), how continuity survives algebra and composition, and how the standard pathological examples show the different kinds of discontinuity; the points belong together because they all work locally, at one point at a time, with the same definition seen from different sides.

points.name: Continuity at a point and on a set: the epsilon-delta definition
points.what: State the definition of f: A -> R being continuous at a point c in A (for every epsilon > 0 there is delta > 0 such that |x - c| < delta and x in A imply |f(x) - f(c)| < epsilon) and of continuity on a set, and explain why c must be in the domain, why f(c) now matters (unlike for limits), and why a restriction of a function can be continuous where the original is not.
outside: nested quantifiers (for all / there exists) and reading their order
epsilon-delta definition of the limit of a function

points.name: Negating continuity
points.what: Write out correctly what it means for f to be discontinuous at c (there is an epsilon > 0 such that for every delta > 0 some x in A with |x - c| < delta has |f(x) - f(c)| >= epsilon), and use this negation to prove simple discontinuities, such as a step function at its jump, directly from the definition.

points.name: Proving continuity from the definition
points.what: Write complete epsilon-delta proofs that particular functions (for example 3x + 1, |x|, x^2 and 1/x at a given point) are continuous, doing scratch work to find delta and noticing when delta depends on both epsilon and the point c.
outside: finding delta by scratch work in epsilon-delta limit proofs
triangle inequality and absolute value inequalities

points.name: Continuity through limits; isolated points
points.what: Prove that at a limit point c of the domain, f is continuous at c exactly when the limit of f(x) as x -> c exists and equals f(c), and that every function is automatically continuous at an isolated point of its domain (so every function on the integers is continuous).
outside: limit points and isolated points of a set
epsilon-delta definition of the limit of a function

points.name: Sequential characterisation of continuity
points.what: Prove that f is continuous at c exactly when f(x_n) -> f(c) for every sequence (x_n) in the domain converging to c, and use this form to move results about sequences over to continuous functions.
outside: sequential criterion for limits of functions

points.name: Proving discontinuity with sequences
points.what: Show that f is discontinuous at c by finding one sequence x_n -> c in the domain with f(x_n) not converging to f(c), and recognise when this is easier than negating the epsilon-delta definition.

points.name: Algebra of continuous functions
points.what: Prove that if f and g are continuous at c then so are kf, f + g, fg and, when g(c) is not 0, f/g, by using the sequential characterisation together with the limit laws instead of redoing epsilon work.
outside: limit laws for sequences or for functions

points.name: Composition of continuous functions
points.what: Prove that if f is continuous at c and g is continuous at f(c) then g o f is continuous at c, both by chaining the epsilon-delta definitions and by sequences, and see why continuity of g at f(c), not just a limit there, is needed.

points.name: Continuity of polynomials, rational functions and familiar functions
points.what: Deduce that polynomials are continuous on R and rational functions on their domains, and build continuity of more complex expressions (such as sqrt(1 + x^2) or sin(x)/x for x not 0) from familiar continuous functions like exp, sin and sqrt, whose continuity is used now and proved when they are defined rigorously.

points.name: Topological form of continuity
points.what: Prove that f: R -> R is continuous exactly when the preimage of every open set is open (equivalently, of every closed set is closed), state the relative version for functions on a subset A (preimages are open relative to A), and use it to see at once that sets like {x : f(x) > 0} are open.
outside: open and closed sets in R
preimage of a set under a function

points.name: Types of discontinuity: removable, jump, essential
points.what: Classify a discontinuity at a limit point c using one-sided limits: removable (the limit exists but differs from f(c) or f(c) is undefined), jump (both one-sided limits exist but differ), and essential (some one-sided limit fails to exist), and identify each type in simple examples.

points.name: sin(1/x) and x sin(1/x) at 0
points.what: Show that sin(1/x) has an essential discontinuity at 0 however it is defined there, while x sin(1/x) has a removable discontinuity that becomes continuous when the value at 0 is set to 0, using sequences for the first and the squeeze theorem for the second.
outside: limit of sin(1/x) as x -> 0 does not exist (two sequences with different limits)
squeeze theorem for limits of functions

points.name: The Dirichlet function: continuous nowhere
points.what: Prove that the function equal to 1 on the rationals and 0 on the irrationals is discontinuous at every point, by choosing sequences of rationals or irrationals converging to the point.
outside: density of the rationals and of the irrationals in R

points.name: x times the Dirichlet function: continuous at exactly one point
points.what: Prove that x times the Dirichlet function is continuous at 0 (take delta = epsilon) and discontinuous everywhere else, and see from it that continuity at a single point says nothing about nearby points.

points.name: Thomae's function: continuous exactly at the irrationals
points.what: Prove that the function equal to 1/q at p/q in lowest terms (q > 0) and 0 at irrationals is discontinuous at every rational and continuous at every irrational, using that only finitely many rationals near a point have denominator at most N; this tests the quantifiers in the definition at their hardest.
outside: density of the irrationals in R
